notes: Adds a `ParseableDiffPrefixes` helper that forces a strippable `a/`/`b/` prefix against noprefix and custom src/dst prefixes, and leaves mnemonicPrefix alone. The parser now strips any single-component prefix, unquotes C-quoted paths, and falls back to `rename to`/`copy to` before the `diff --git` line. It also adds the prefix override to the worktree-file and stash diffs, which previously lacked it. Hidden tests pass, but the `diff --git` splitting logic and any new parser tests are cut off and could not be checked; the visible test edits only update expected argv lists.

This is a sound fix. It adds a `ParseableDiffPrefixes()` builder that forces `noprefix=false` plus `srcPrefix`/`dstPrefix` on every diff lazygit parses, leaves `mnemonicPrefix` alone, and generalizes the parser to strip any single-component prefix. It also adds `rename to`/`copy to` handling, unquoted and without prefix stripping, correctly. Hidden tests pass, but the truncated diff hides the `diff --git` splitting logic and any new parser tests. The visible test changes are mostly mechanical argv updates, and the change to `commit_file_loader` (a `--name-status` command) is unnecessary but harmless.

On each GC this patch scans the exemplar storage for series whose newest exemplar is at or after minValidTime, keeps those series in the head and drops their chunks. That is plausible, but it races with exemplar appends made after the scan, assumes the newest exemplar is also the maximum timestamp, and fails all three hidden tests plus the package suite.

The approach is plausible: before GC it builds a set of series labels that still have an exemplar at or after minValidTime, then keeps those series in both gc and gcSeries while releasing their chunks. However, it fails all three hidden tests and breaks the package suite, so key requirements likely do not hold. It also has an append-vs-GC race because the set is computed before the stripe locks are taken, it rebuilds a label-string map on every GC, and it duplicates the stale and histogram accounting in two places.
